title: How to play
intro:
**Horseless Carriage: How to play**

A guided first year at the works, against two rival industrialists, Robin and Sam.

steps.welcome: Welcome to the works, director. Nobody knows yet what a horseless carriage should be. Fast? Safe? Pretty? Each year we research new technology, build it into our factory, and sell cars to buyers who want certain specs. And every year the public changes its mind about what matters.
steps.goal: Money is the only scoreboard. Every dollar we earn shows beside our name. Time is kept by the punch clock: the timecard moves down as the years pass, and when it runs out, the richest company wins.
steps.market: This is the market. Its sixty-four squares are niches, and each car standing on one is a buyer waiting for the right machine. The board is cut into four quadrants of sixteen niches. The shading marks four price segments, cheap at the bottom-left and dear at the top-right. A price marker shows what a buyer in that segment pays.
steps.axes: Two research tracks lie along the board: today the public cares about safety and reliability. The axes beside them say how much of each a column and a row demands. The bottom-left niche asks for nothing. The top-right niche asks for the most on both. The black arrow points at the track that will leave the market at the end of this year.
steps.tracks: The other three research tracks wait off the board. Each track has six slots, and each slot pictures a technology station we could learn to build. This is your marker on each track. The innovation markers count how far research has run ahead on each track.
steps.office: This is the planning office. Gantt charts are planning, and they decide who chooses a focus first. The focus track sets the order for the year: engineering on the left, sales on the right. Below it is last year's focus. Assembly capacity, beside your name, is how many cars each production line builds a year. Your place in this year's engineering order and sales order shows there too.
steps.factory: And this is your factory floor. Everything we build must connect to the loading bay. Your two departments are already on the floor: research gives you research steps, and planning earns Gantt charts.
steps.supply-cards: Stations, production lines and departments come from this shared supply, and there are only so many of each. Your market cards bring new buyers to the market later in the year.
steps.place-departments: The departments must touch the loading bay, or a tile that does. Where they stand is fine. Tap Done to open the works.
steps.others-setup: Robin and Sam open their works too.
steps.research: Each year begins in the laboratory. Every research department gives you one step. You may move any marker on any track, even a rival's, but never the same marker twice. Or you may raise your own assembly capacity instead, with the Capacity button. Some spaces show a punch clock: reaching one moves the timecard down, and the end comes closer.
steps.research-space: Your research department gives you one step. Tap your marker's space on the reliability track.
steps.research-marker: Three markers stand there. Tap your own.
steps.research-done: Your reliability marker now stands on the chassis. From today you may build a chassis, and point a reliability indicator at it.
steps.others-research-robin: Robin takes a step on the safety track.
steps.others-research-sam: Sam tries something new: a step on the design track, off the board.
steps.focus: Now the focus. Players choose in order of Gantt charts, most first. The focus track runs from engineering on the left to sales on the right. Slot 1 builds first, plays cards first, and holds the best patents: it may build anything another player has researched. The highest open slot sells first, and wins ties at the end; with three of us, slots 4 and 5 stay closed. Taking a slot spends all your Gantt charts back to zero; passing keeps them, and you take what is left.
steps.focus-do: You have the most Gantt charts, so you choose first. Take slot 1, engineering.
steps.others-focus-robin: Robin takes slot 3, the far right: sales. Robin will sell first this year.
steps.others-focus-sam: Sam passes and keeps a Gantt chart. Sam takes the slot that is left, slot 2.
steps.confirm-setup: Confirm, and the works are open.
steps.build: Now we build. The Add gallery below opens with everything you may build this year: tap a piece, and it lands on your floor for you to drag into place. Every tile must sit on black floor, never on a loading bay, and never on another tile. Everyone builds at the same time, each in their own works.
steps.add-mainline: A factory starts with a production line. Tap the car mainline in the Add gallery.
steps.place-mainline: Drag the mainline to the ringed spot, beside the loading bay.
steps.mainline: The mainline builds cars. Each of its four sides belongs to one manufacturing step, marked A, B, C and D.
steps.add-dealer: Cars need a dealer to sell them. Add your small dealership.
steps.rotate-dealer: Turn it on its side with Rotate.
steps.place-dealer: Now drag it against the mainline's left side. A dealer must touch a mainline, and a mainline must touch a dealer.
steps.zones: Stations go beside the mainline side of their own step. The chassis is an A station, so it goes on the A side. Each step has its own hatching, and stations, indicators and mainline sides of the same step form a manufacturing zone. Two identical stations may never share a zone. Every station needs a spec indicator pointing at it, and that is what gives your cars their specs.
steps.place-chassis: Drag it below the mainline, against its A side.
steps.add-spec: Now give it a reliability indicator. Each research slot you reach allows one indicator on that station. Tap Add spec.
steps.place-spec: The indicator lands on a free square touching the chassis, here in the ringed corner. You could drag it to any square that touches the chassis.
steps.add-marketing: One more. A marketing department lets your dealer reach further into the market. Add it.
steps.place-marketing: And drag it below the dealer. Marketing must touch a dealer.
steps.expansion: One last thing. Each year you also add a floor expansion. It came with its own loading bay, and the strip beside that bay must stay clear. We can build on it from next year.
steps.done-build: Nothing is outlined in pink, so everything is legal. Tap Done.
steps.others-build: Robin and Sam finish their factories.
steps.brochures: Now the brochures go to print. Each planning department adds a Gantt chart, and reaching ten punches the clock. Each dealer publishes its specs: the indicators in its mainline's zones. Each marketing department beside a dealer makes its market window bigger: that is the frame it lays on the market to sell. Later in the game, research tracks that leave the market set minimum specifications, and a dealer that misses any minimum sells nothing at all. The faint rectangle on the market shows every niche your dealer can reach.
steps.sell: Then we sell, in sales order: the rightmost focus first. On your turn you place a dealer's window on the market, where no niche asks for more than your specs. It may hang off the edge, and it may overlap other windows. Then you sell to every buyer you can supply in one niche inside it. You can sell as many cars a year as your assembly capacity, per mainline.
steps.others-sell-robin: Robin sells first, from the sales end of the focus track: one car, six dollars.
steps.others-sell-sam: Then Sam sells one car too.
steps.sell-window: Your turn. Drag your dealer's window onto the ringed spot. Your dealer has one reliability and no safety, so it may only cover niches that ask for no more than that. Then confirm.
steps.sell-niche: Two buyers sit inside your window. Your mainline builds one car a year, so you sell to one of them. Pick either.
steps.sold: Six dollars, beside your name. That was your mainline's whole capacity for the year. Selling goes round in rounds until nobody can sell any more, and nobody can pass while they still could.
steps.finish: Is the game over? Not yet. When the timecard reaches the last space of the punch clock, it flips over. The game ends after the year in which the timecard flips, or after the seventh year, when the floor expansions are all used.
steps.expectations: Now the public changes its mind. The track the black arrow points at leaves the market and goes under the others. Its minimum specification rises by one, and its tile appears beside the market: from now on nobody sells a car without it. Remember Sam's design step? The most innovative off-board track, the one where research has run furthest ahead, takes its place. On a tie, the track with the marker furthest ahead wins, and then the top track. The arrow turns to the other track, for next year.
steps.grow: Last, demand grows. Each of us plays one market card face down beside a quadrant. A card shows sparks: places in that quadrant where the public is warming to a car. A card can only be played once you have placed as many floor expansions as the year printed on it.
steps.play-card: Play this card. It shows one car spark and one punch clock.
steps.play-quadrant: Put it beside quadrant one, where your dealer can reach.
steps.reveal: The cards turn over, quadrant by quadrant. Played cards are gone for good. Each spark lands on its niche and stays there, and every punch clock moves the timecard down. Every spark brings one new buyer each year, up to two per spark. Then the neutral deck, which belongs to nobody, adds a few more buyers. And the prices are set again: the dearest segment that has buyers takes the six dollar marker.
steps.year-two: That was a whole year. Look at your dealer: it has no safety, and safety now has a minimum of one. So next year, research safety and build a brake, or your dealer sells nothing. Next year the expansion is part of your floor. Stations you built stay where they are, and keep their indicators even if your access is lost, but they can take new indicators as your research grows. With several dealers, you may place several windows before selling from earlier ones. Where two of your windows cover a niche, you choose which dealer sells. At the end of each year the windows come home.
steps.game-end: The game ends after the year in which the timecard flips, or after year seven. Then the richest company wins. If two are tied, the one with the higher sales focus wins.
steps.full-game: We played the introductory rules. In the full game, trucks and sports cars come to market too: a truck pays one dollar more, and a sports car two, but each needs its own mainline.
steps.finish-tutorial: The works are yours, director. Build boldly, sell hard. If I can dream it, you can do it!

hints.place-departments: Tap Done in the bar below.
hints.research-space: Tap the highlighted space on the safety track.
hints.research-marker: Tap your red marker in the gallery.
hints.focus-do: Tap slot 1 on the focus track.
hints.add-mainline: Tap Add in the bar below, then the car mainline.
hints.place-mainline: Drag the mainline onto the ringed spot.
hints.add-dealer: Tap Add, then the small dealership.
hints.place-dealer: Drag the dealer onto the ringed spot.
hints.place-chassis: Drag the chassis onto the ringed spot.
hints.place-spec: Drag the indicator onto the ringed square.
hints.add-marketing: Tap Add, then the marketing department.
hints.place-marketing: Drag it onto the ringed spot.
hints.sell-window: Drag the window above the board onto the ringed spot, then tap Confirm.
hints.sell-niche: Tap one of the highlighted niches inside your window.
hints.play-quadrant: Tap the ringed space beside quadrant one.
